statement: There is no universal bound of the form integral |E_rho exp(it z^T H z)|^2 dt <= C |det H|^(-1/2) over arbitrary planar probability densities rho<=1 when H is indefinite. For q(x,y)=xy, R>e, delta=1/log R and rho=1 on {1<=x<=R,0<=y<=delta/x}, rho has mass one while q has density log R on (0,delta), so its L2-square is log R. This is not a counterexample to QFORM because rho is a dependent joint density; it blocks forgetting original-coordinate product provenance in the indefinite two-dimensional cross-kernel branch.
replacement: Use the product-preserving scalar L4 square-phase estimate on two independent ORIGINAL coordinates; in that coordinate-separable kernel scope the report proves ||p_Q||inf <= (9/2) Delta^(-1/3)|ac|^(-1/6).
